We all love a good thrill from time to time, but who says it needs to come from a screen? Some of the greatest thrillers began on the page as books. A beloved genre, they trigger an exciting "fight or flight" rush from the safety of an armchair. Thrillers let us experience fear, danger, and intense suspense without any real-world risk, challenging our brains to piece together clues, test our instincts, and figure out the twist before the characters do.

Some incredible thrillers have come and gone over time, but the 2010s saw a resurgence of greats. We’re here to celebrate 10, one from each year of the decade. From murder mysteries to domestic dramas, these books gave us the sensation we seek from the genre. While some brilliant novels from the decade missed out, each year saw major battles for the top spot.

1
'The Last Days of Ptolemy Grey' by Walter Mosley (2010)

blocks.c: The book cover of 'The Last Days of Ptolemy Grey' by Walter Mosley.

blocks.x: A moving and suspenseful story, The Last Days of Ptolemy Grey tells the story of a 91-year-old man named Ptolemy Grey who suffers from severe dementia and uses a temporary memory-restoring treatment to investigate his grand-nephew Reggie's murder. A 17-year-old orphan named Robyn moves in to help care for him, pushing him to reengage with the world. Ptolemy agrees to take an unapproved, experimental treatment that trades a shortened lifespan for a brief window of vivid mental clarity, using it to track down Reggie’s killer. Exploring the fragility of the human mind, the pain of fading memories, and the heavy toll of untreated dementia, The Last Days of Ptolemy Grey highlights the complex dynamics of family loyalty, grief, and an old man's desperate bid to right past wrongs.

Written by Walter Mosley, the novel redefines the genre by replacing mean streets with the labyrinth of a failing human mind. Instead of a detective racing through a city, it’s the 91-year-old doing the heavy lifting. Rooted in reality, as Mosley served as a caretaker for his parents, the story’s authenticity regarding Alzheimer's and dementia is quite raw. The book transforms a cacophony of disjointed memories into a symphony of remembrance. A truly tender tale, The Last Days of Ptolemy Grey became the perfect vessel for an Apple TV series. Consisting of six episodes, Mosley created an underrated miniseries starring Samuel L. Jackson as Ptolemy Grey and Dominique Fishback as Robyn.

2
'Before I Go to Sleep' by S.J. Watson (2011)

blocks.c: Before I Go to Sleep Book Cover

blocks.x: S.J. Watson's first novel, Before I Go to Sleep, is a psychological thriller about Christine Lucas, who wakes up every morning with severe anterograde amnesia, meaning her memory resets completely every time she falls asleep. Her life is mediated by a man who claims to be her husband, but secretly working with neuropsychologist Dr. Nash, Christine begins keeping a journal to record her daily discoveries and thoughts, bypassing her memory loss. Her written entries eventually reveal a terrifying note to herself: "DON'T TRUST BEN." An enthralling thrill ride, Before I Go to Sleep uses a high-concept memory-loss premise to create intense paranoia, claustrophobia, and the ultimate test of trust.

Before I Go to Sleep forces the audience to trust Christine as she begins to question her surroundings and the individuals around her. Because Christine cannot trust her own memory, she cannot verify if the people around her — her husband and her doctor — are telling her the truth. It pushes the audience to experience her exact confusion and helplessness. The novel asks a haunting philosophical question: Are we defined by our memories? Before I Go to Sleep helped fuel the psychological thriller boom of the 2010s, so much so that it was adapted into a film starring Nicole Kidman, Colin Firth, and Mark Strong.

blocks.c: Book cover for Gillian Flynn's Gone Girl

blocks.x: If there’s one thriller that defined the decade, look no further than Gone Girl by Gillian Flynn. Most certainly the book your mom read at the pool, beach, or lake, the domestic psychological thriller showcases a seemingly perfect marriage that turns toxic when Amy Dunne mysteriously disappears on their fifth wedding anniversary, framing her husband Nick for her murder. The story alternates between Nick’s present-day struggle to prove his innocence and Amy’s past diary entries detailing their relationship, only for a massive twist to shake up the narrative. Gone Girl explores the psychological need to present a version of oneself to please others while satirizing the 24-hour news cycle’s obsession with convicting people in the court of public opinion.

Gone Girl shattered traditional genre tropes by reinventing the unreliable narrator through its invention of domestic noir. The story centers on calculated deception. Both main characters weaponize their flaws and manipulate the reader, making objective truth impossible to find. Flynn exposes the dark underbelly of modern relationships and marriages. Love is out the window as Nick and Amy wage a psychological battle. Amy Dunne redefined anti-heroines by embodying unvarnished rage and chilling brilliance rather than playing a damsel archetype. The New York Times bestseller was given the movie treatment starring Ben Affleck and Rosamund Pike. ​​​​​​​

blocks.c: The book cover of 'The Silent Wife' by A.S.A. Harrison.

blocks.x: Sometimes, all you need is one masterpiece to define your legacy. The only novel published before her death, The Silent Wife by A.S.A. Harrison, chronicles the slow, dark unraveling of a 20-year common-law marriage in Chicago. Jodi Brett, a 45-year-old psychotherapist who likes routine, avoids conflict, and lives largely in denial, and Todd Gilbert, a self-absorbed, wealthy property developer in his 40s who is a serial cheater, reach a breaking point when he gets his best friend's young daughter, Natasha, pregnant. Feeling as though she has nothing left to lose, Jodi calmly and methodically plans Todd's murder. The Silent Wife is a slow-burning psychological character study that examines the dark side of complacency and the tipping point of a toxic relationship.

Rather than litter the story with plot twists for the sake of shock, Harrison allows the dissolving of a relationship to devolve as it collapses into a brutal outcome. With an immediate hook that alerts you to where Jodi descends, The Silent Wife becomes a march toward murder rather than a question of what might happen next. Harrison uses alternating he-said/she-said chapters to expose the deep divide between the two parties. A more plausible story than its predecessor from the previous year, The Silent Wife continued the wave of domestic dramas. A film adaptation was optioned and was to star Nicole Kidman, but it sadly never came to fruition. ​​​​​​​

A standout thriller that places the action within a quaint coastal Australian neighborhood, Big Little Lies is a highly addictive mystery. Written by Liane Moriarty, the thriller follows three mothers whose lives unravel over six months, culminating in a school trivia night murder. When single mom and newcomer Jane Chapman’s son Ziggy is falsely accused of bullying a classmate, the three women are forced into a close alliance. Tensions rise as Jane realizes that wealthy wife Celeste Wright’s abusive husband, Perry, may have played a pivotal role in her past. A story about the hidden darkness behind perfect domestic facades and the lies people tell themselves to survive, Big Little Lies is a juicy thriller that blends sharp domestic dark comedy with a high-stakes murder mystery.

With an addictive hook that draws you in immediately, Big Little Lies keeps the victim and the killer a secret until the very end. It lets the reader deduce who it could be, since anyone could be the culprit. The suburban noir subverts the concept of the happy suburban family by exposing the dark, violent truths hidden behind wealthy, perfect facades. Moriarty weaves heavy topics into the narrative in an engaging way without ever being gratuitous. A female-led page-turner, Big Little Lies made the leap to the small screen for a two-season hit starring Reese Witherspoon, Nicole Kidman, and Shailene Woodley. The series moved beyond the novel and shifted the action to Monterey, California, yet kept Moriarty’s DNA present.

6
'The Girl on the Train' by Paula Hawkins (2015)

blocks.c: Book cover of "The Girl on the Train" by Paula Hawkins

blocks.x: Image via courtesy of Penguin Books

What happens on the train does not stay on the train. In The Girl on the Train by Paula Hawkins, Rachel, a struggling alcoholic, rides the same train every day, watching a nearby couple she calls "Jess and Jason" and imagining their perfect life. When “Jess,” known as Megan Hipwell, goes missing, Rachel is pulled into the missing-person investigation, only to discover the truth might actually involve her. The Girl on the Train tackles deep themes of trauma, projecting false fantasies onto strangers' lives, gaslighting, and domestic abuse. Hawkins’ thriller helped redefine the unreliable-narrator drama.

Rachel is not your average spokesperson. She’s an unemployed alcoholic who suffers from frequent blackouts. This forces readers to question every memory, doubt every clue, and wonder if Rachel herself committed a crime during her blackouts. Through dizzying uncertainty, the narrative keeps readers on their toes as nothing is truly what it seems. To truly push the confusion, Hawkins shifts perspective between Rachel, Megan, and Anna, Rachel’s ex’s new wife. This allows crucial information to unfold slowly, building tension and layering deceit before the explosive final twist. The story of voyeurism is quite accessible, as we’ve all been Rachel. A mundane trip on public transport taps into the universal habit of wondering about the lives of total strangers. The novel was adapted into a stage play and a film starring Emily Blunt, Rebecca Ferguson, and Justin Theroux. ​​​​​​​

blocks.c: The book cover for 'Dark Matter' by Blake Crouch.

blocks.x: When it comes to defining sci-fi thrillers of the decade, look no further than Dark Matter by Blake Crouch. The story follows college physics teacher Jason Dessen, who is abducted by an alternate version of himself and wakes up in a parallel world where he is not a simple professor but a celebrated scientific genius who never married his wife, Daniela, and whose son, Charlie, was never born. Jason must navigate a mind-bending multiverse to return to his true family. A strong use of the multiverse mechanic, Dark Matter explores the road not taken and how a single past decision branches out into entirely different lives.

Crouch’s thriller stands out as a modern masterpiece through its tight mix of high-concept quantum mechanics and an intense emotional center about human regret and the power of choice. The novel is quick and punchy, with Crouch using short chapters to move through the timelines without excessive narrative fat. Instead of bogging down the plot with dense jargon, the novel translates complex ideas into a high-stakes tool. It’s not about the specificity of science, but rather its consequences. By tapping into the universal "what if" anxieties, the story is quite accessible. The novel served as the basis of the hit Apple TV series starring Joel Edgerton and Jennifer Connelly. Now in its second season, the series has officially surpassed the novel. ​​​​​​​

Reinventing the classic whodunnit of the Golden Age of British detective fiction, Anthony Horowitz’s Magpie Murders launched the Susan Ryeland series. Book editor Susan Ryeland is thrust into a murder mystery when difficult and arrogant author Alan Conway is found dead in an apparent suicide. As Susan digs deeper into Conway, she discovers that the secrets and clues hidden in his manuscript mirror the real-life malice and hidden motives of the people around him.

Magpie Murders satirizes the complex, often toxic relationships between authors, editors, and publishers and the ambition that comes with it through the lens of retro crime stories. A smart work of metafiction, Magpie Murders’ mystery within a mystery serves as an addictive page-turner. The parallel puzzle allows the reader to engage in the investigation alongside Susan. The inner 1955 story starring detective Atticus Pünd pays loving homage to classic tropes reminiscent of Agatha Christie. Horowitz’s ability to tap into the past style through a modern lens proves the hunger for the genre has never waned. The framing device allows him the brilliant opportunity to explore the psychology of mystery writers. The drama was adapted into a six-part miniseries starring Lesley Manville as Susan. ​​​​​​​

blocks.c: The Perfect Nanny by Leila Slimani book cover on black background.

blocks.x: Leïla Slimani taps into every mother’s waking nightmare in her 2018 thriller The Perfect Nanny. Initially appearing to be a dream caregiver, Louise and the family grow aggressively dependent on one another; hidden financial debts, severe isolation, mental instability, and mounting obsessive boundaries begin to fracture the household. The Perfect Nanny explores the unequal dynamics and tensions between affluent employers and struggling domestic workers, as well as the pressure and guilt placed on working mothers.

The Perfect Nanny subverts pulp conventions by turning a terrifying tragedy into a critique of class, power, and modern motherhood. Slimani opens with the instant hook: "The baby is dead." From there, you’re immediately aware that Louise has murdered the children — it’s a matter of discovering why. The narrative is truly exhausting and intense, keeping you glued to how the relationships devolve into chaos. Slimani brilliantly exposes the hypocrisies of affluent employers who invite a caretaker intimately into their lives while maintaining rigid, elitist social distances. Published in English in 2018, The Perfect Nanny previously won France’s Prix Goncourt. The novel has been adapted into an upcoming HBO series starring Nicole Kidman and Maya Erskine. ​​​​​​​

blocks.c: Book cover of 'The Silent Patient' by Alex Michaelides

blocks.x: In Alex Michaelides’ debut novel The Silent Patient, Alicia Berenson is a famous London painter who shoots her fashion-photographer husband, Gabriel, five times in the face and then never speaks another word. Her absolute muteness turns the tragedy into a massive public obsession, and she is confined to a secure psychiatric facility called the Grove. Through heavy imagery of Alcestis by Euripides to mirror Alicia's psychological state and sacrifice, The Silent Patient relies on a masterful twist to turn the narrative into something much richer than a doctor helping a patient.

A high-concept thriller, The Silent Patient is filled with dark psychological depth and a jaw-dropping twist you’ll never see coming. The story alternates between Theo's active investigation and Alicia’s past diary entries, forcing readers to question both doctor and patient.
